question: A recent report by the French intelligence services analysed the architecture of the Muslim Brotherhood’s (MB) European network, highlighting how the organisation uses educational institutions to spread integralist ideologies.

These include the Bayan Institute of San Giovanni Lupatoto (Verona), chaired by Tareq al-Suwaidan, who is affiliated to the MB (as recognised by the Italian Ministry of the Interior) and banned by both Belgium and the United States for his extremist and anti-Semitic positions.

According to leading academics, as well as the security services of several Member States, the MB pursues a political project aimed at the Islamisation of the public space, which runs counter to the constitutional principles underpinning European democracies.

The MB has so far enjoyed formal recognition by the EU institutions, confirmed, inter alia, by a meeting held in November 2021 between Commissioner Dalli and representatives of FEMYSO (the MB’s youth organisation), and by FEMYSO’s participation in the European Youth Event held at Parliament in Strasbourg in June 2023. In light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission agree with the views expressed in the above-mentioned report on the dangers posed to European democracy by the MB through institutions like the one in Verona?
Will it cease all dialogue with FEMYSO, the Federation of Islamic Organisations in Europe and other bodies linked to the MB?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.9.2025) The Commission would like to refer the Honourable Member to previous replies to written questions on the subject of the influence of the Muslim Brotherhood1.

The Commission is aware of the report of the French Ministry of Interior and closely follows the evolving risk linked to organisations trying to unduly influence the European institutions, including radical and extremist non-state actors, as well as interference from third countries. The Commission values information provided by the Member States and takes note of the recent French report.

It is the responsibility of the Member States to take the necessary measures, including by addressing the national courts, in case of substantiated breaches of the law by an association registered under their jurisdiction taking into account the need to respect freedom of speech, freedom of association and freedom of religion and belief as well as the need to preserve an enabling framework for civil society and human rights defenders.
